images.title: A playground with a compass
images.purpose: Show that on a picture with a compass the top is north, the bottom is south, the right is east and the left is west, using four playground things in a two by two pattern.
images.composition: A playground in a green border with a swing at the top left, a slide at the top right, a sandpit at the bottom left and a seesaw at the bottom right; four arrows run round them, east, south, west and north; a compass card is at the top right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, flat colours, thin dark #2B2B2B outlines (3 px). PLAYGROUND: ONE rounded rectangle (corner radius 24 px), white fill, with a green #009E73 border 10 px thick, from x 340 to x 1116 and from y 70 to y 746. Inside it FOUR things in a two by two pattern, the left two centred at x 534 and the right two centred at x 922, the top two centred at y 225 and the bottom two centred at y 575, each about 170 px wide and 130 px tall: the SWING at the top left, one teal #0072B2 top bar with two slanted teal legs, two thin dark ropes hanging from the bar and ONE amber #E69F00 seat; the SLIDE at the top right, one ladder with two teal #0072B2 rails and 3 rungs on the left, one small platform at the top and ONE long sloped amber #E69F00 ramp going down to the right; the SANDPIT at the bottom left, ONE flat rounded rectangle (150 by 110 px) filled amber #E69F00 with a teal #0072B2 border, and ONE small teal bucket (a trapezoid 30 px wide) in it; the SEESAW at the bottom right, ONE long plank (170 by 14 px) in reddish purple #CC79A7 tilted a little, resting on ONE teal #0072B2 triangle, with ONE small handle bar at each end of the plank. NAME LABELS in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (36 px), each centred above its thing: Swing at x 534 and y 125, Slide at x 922 and y 125, Sandpit at x 534 and y 470, Seesaw at x 922 and y 470. FOUR ARROWS, each a green #009E73 line 8 px thick with one arrow head, with a word beside it in dark bold (36 px): east from x 640 to x 816 at y 225, pointing right, with the word east centred at x 728 and y 190; south from y 305 to y 430 at x 922, pointing down, with the word south centred at x 1000 and y 368; west from x 830 to x 645 at y 575, pointing left, with the word west centred at x 738 and y 540; north from y 430 to y 305 at x 534, pointing up, with the word north centred at x 455 and y 368. COMPASS CARD outside the playground at the top right: a square card with rounded corners (corner radius 14 px), 170 by 170 px, from x 1196 to x 1366 and from y 70 to y 240, white fill, dark #2B2B2B outline 6 px, with a cross of two thin double headed dark arrows (4 px) inside it: one vertical from y 125 to y 185 at x 1281 and one horizontal from x 1252 to x 1312 at y 155; the letter N in dark bold (38 px) centred at x 1281 and y 102 (top), S in dark bold at x 1281 and y 208 (bottom), W in dark bold at x 1226 and y 155 (left) and E in red #D55E00 bold at x 1340 and y 155 (right). In all: 4 playground things, 4 name labels, 4 arrows with 4 words, 1 compass card. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: On a picture with a compass, above is north, below is south, the right is east and the left is west: the slide is east of the swing, the seesaw is south of the slide, the sandpit is west of the seesaw and the swing is north of the sandpit.
images.description: A playground with a swing, a slide, a sandpit and a seesaw in a two by two pattern, four arrows labelled east, south, west and north, and a compass card.
images.context: Concept image for Reading Directions on a Picture. It follows the idea of the camp picture in your maths book (a picture with a compass whose N is at the top) and uses this concept's own playground.
images.teaching_notes: Start from one thing, then follow the arrow named by the word. The compass says N is at the top, so up is north. The slip to watch: reading east and west the wrong way round, as if the left of the picture were east.

image_decisions.why: The two by two playground with a compass makes above, below, right and left into north, south, east and west, and the four arrows make each answer countable.
